rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 185.4): oval finished 3 of 20 trials, s-bend and slalom finished 0 of 20 each, and every failure was off_track. max_error sits at 0.058 to 0.064, right at the off-track limit of 0.06 m (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06). rms_error is small (0.016 to 0.023), so the robot tracks well in steady state and loses the line on bends. Steering oscillation rose on the s-bend (0.29) and slalom (0.19), and control_effort on the s-bend (8.8) shows strong corrective steering. The failure is a lag problem: the sensors are only 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the controller reacts late at speed. Two changes address this. (1) Move the sensors forward to y = 0.07 so the controller sees the bend earlier and gains phase lead. (2) Raise kd from 0.5 to 0.8 to damp the faster corrections, and lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.2 to give the steering more room on tight bends. kp moves only slightly, from 4.0 to 4.5, because the s-bend control effort is already high. The sensor spread is widened to x = ±0.05 (weights ±2, ±1, 0 unchanged) so the signal responds to a larger lateral offset before the robot reaches the edge. Wheel geometry, mass and line_loss are unchanged to isolate the effect of sensing and damping. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error below 0.055 and progress above 0.5 on the s-bend. The main risk is that base_speed 1.2 is too slow to finish the oval within 3 s. Hypotheses for next iteration: if the robot still exits the first bend, the sensor lead is not enough and I should move the sensors further forward or raise kp. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4, kd is too high or the lead is too aggressive. If completion_time is over 3 s on the oval, base_speed needs to rise again. Measurements requested: completion, progress and completion_time for speed; max_error and line_loss_events for recovery; steering_oscillation and control_effort for gain stability.
